messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: speeding up compilation
parts:
On 8/14/12 6:41 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:

> This is probably impossible, butï¿½ if there are any clever
> ways of getting compilation to be faster, that would be great!

We've already done the first-order things.

The main problem is that the compiler settings that produce
fast code are themselves slow.

Overall, with the size models you're looking at,
compiling at -O0 level and running would probably
take less time overall than compiling at -O3 level (-O is
for optimization level, with 0 minimum and 3 the max that
matters).

Here are two ways we might speedup compilation:

1. More precompilation into object files.

Pros: faster compiles
Cons: it makes the code more difficult to manage
and less flexible by requiring redundancy
and preinstation of templates


2. More targeted imports.

Pros: faster compiles because less code to read
Cons: may defeat precompiled headers


- Bob
